transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-18
Start: 10:30 AM PDT / 17:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sam Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), John Lee (Acme Head of Platform), Maya Torres (Acme Security Architect), Evan Park (Acme Cloud Engineer)

Summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Quick discovery to understand Acme's private deployment requirements for Redwood Private; focus on VPC networking (peering vs PrivateLink), region constraints, IP allowlists, KMS/HSM integration, and compliance questions. Next step: checklist/pricing + benchmark run.

[00:00] Sam: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll just do a quick intros, I'm Sam Hayes, AE on the Redwood side, with me is Priya our SE, and then we'll go through your architecture and requirements for a private VPC deployment.
[00:15] John: yeah hi, john lee here, head of platform at Acme Robotics. we run multi-region infra for our fleet mgmt system; looking at running model inference internally, want to evaluate Redwood Private.
[00:28] Priya: thanks john, quick q to start — are you leaning toward a dedicated host within Redwood managed infra or fully private inside your VPC? or hybrid?
[00:40] John: primary preference is fully private — we need traffic to stay inside our VPCs in eu-west-1 due to data residency and regulatory reasons, we may consider dedicated later for burst.
[00:52] Maya: and from security, we need KMS integration with our HSM, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SSO via SAML, and SOC2 plus export controls docs.
[01:05] Sam: got it; so Private deployment it is. priya, can you run through the two common networking patterns we typically see — VPC peering/transit vs PrivateLink/private endpoints?
[01:20] Priya: yeah sure — generally customers do one of: 1) VPC Peering or Transit Gateway peering where Redwood runs a VPC in the customer's account or we peer across accounts; 2) AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints where we expose the service via ENIs and you hit it via private endpoints. each has tradeoffs — peering can be simpler for north-south routing but transit/cross-account routing may need route tables updates, private endpoints give more controlled access but require ENIs in subnets and cross-zone considerations.
[01:50] Evan: quick clarifying q — do you require that Redwood sit in our account, or can you manage the attachments from your side?
[01:58] Priya: we support both patterns. we can run a customer-dedicated VPC that you peer with, or we can create interface endpoints and provide you DNS names to resolve privately. for some enterprise customers we provide a bring-your-own-account option where our infra runs in your account under a deployment recipe.
[02:15] John: ok, aws-focused for now. region constraint: we must be in eu-west-1 only, not eu-central-1. any limitations if you host in a single AZ vs multi-AZ?
[02:26] Priya: we recommend multi-AZ for SLA. latency for your fleet mgmt use case — what's the P95 target?
[02:34] John: aim for p95 < 250ms for short single-turn generation (~50 tokens) and throughput of ~2k concurrent requests (mostly smaller prompts).
[02:44] Priya: that helps. for that profile we recommend a cluster with GPU instances spread across at least two AZs and a regional load balancer — we can do cross-AZ peering or use a regional service endpoint. you'll want sufficient ENI quotas.
[02:58] Maya: about egress — we need to ensure no data is going to public internet and all outgoing egress is controlled. how do you handle downstream calls or model telemetry?
[03:09] Sam: good — telemetry and logs can be forwarded via your Kinesis/CloudWatch subscription or we can write to S3 endpoints in your account. for private deployments we do not route inference traffic over public internet; any control-plane comms can be optionally routed via a management tunnel but that's configurable.
[03:25] Evan: will we see fixed IP ranges for the service? our firewall team needs CIDR blocks for allowlisting.
[03:33] Priya: yes, if you use PrivateLink we expose ENIs in your subnets so allowlist is internal. if we peer, we'll share the Redwood VPC CIDR and recommended route table entries. we provide the set of IP ranges used by the control plane and data plane — usually a small set per deployment.
[03:50] John: and what about cross-account role access for S3 and KMS? we want to ensure data at rest is encrypted with our customer-managed KMS (CMK) in our account.
[04:02] Priya: we integrate with customer KMS for key wrap; we'll request an IAM role to accept encrypted objects or we can use envelope encryption where keys never leave your control. for HSM-backed CMKs we verify policies. file access patterns — do you want logs and artifacts written into your S3 or ours?
[04:20] Maya: put logs into our account only. audit trail must be ours. also want AWS CloudTrail integration and real-time alerting to our SIEM.
[04:29] Sam: that's standard for our Private customers — we forward access logs to your S3 and CloudTrail; we can also push to a syslog endpoint. we'll include that in the deployment checklist.
[04:41] John: on the networking specifics — we use Transit Gateway already for inter-VPC connectivity; will Redwood integrate with TGW peering?
[04:50] Priya: yes, we have customers who connect via Transit Gateway. typical pattern: Redwood VPC peers into your TGW attachment and you manage routing. note that TGW transitive routing has some constraints so we work with your network team on route propagation and security groups.
[05:05] Evan: any requirements on IP addressing? our subnets are /20; we can carve out /24s for endpoints.
[05:12] Priya: that should be fine; we'll ask for a /27 or /26 per AZ for ENIs depending on scale. we'll include recommended subnet sizing in checklist.
[05:22] Maya: compliance — SOC2 is okay, but we also need to confirm where the crash dumps or intermediate caches are stored, e.g., KV cache and prefix caching. can those be disabled or routed to our storage?
[05:36] Priya: yes — KV cache is part of runtime optimization; for Private deployments we can configure cache to be ephemeral and ensure eviction, and logs/traces can be stored in your S3. we can also disable external telemetry if required.
[05:50] John: there was an earlier note about fallback behaviors — if capacity is constrained do you fail open to hosted or degrade to smaller quantized models?
[05:59] Sam: for Private we can configure fallback policies. options: degrade to a lower-cost quantized variant that runs on the same infra, or route to Redwood Dedicated/Hosted in another region as an optional fallback. both require explicit sign-off because of data residency.
[06:14] Evan: how does auth work for the endpoints? we use short-lived certs and mTLS between services internally.
[06:21] Priya: we support mutual TLS for service-to-service connections and token-based auth for SDKs. in private deployments we can wire up mTLS using your CA or use short-lived certs managed by us with rotation.
[06:33] Maya: SSO — we integrate with Okta SAML, right? we need role-based access and audit logs per user.
[06:40] Sam: yes SAML/Okta supported, RBAC at resource level, and we can export audit logs showing which user triggered a call. Priya will share the RBAC model doc.
[06:51] Priya: quick note on region-specific constraints — you mentioned eu-west-1 only. we have infra in eu-west-1 but some optional tooling currently relies on us-east-1 for management plane; for fully isolated private deployments we can localize everything but there may be a small control-plane call to our central orchestration — we can provide an option to run a fully customer-managed control plane in your account if needed for compliance.
[07:18] John: ok that's important. can you clarify latency implications if control plane is remote?
[07:24] Priya: control plane latency doesn't affect inference path; inference is served in-region. control-plane operations like deployments, logs ingestion are async and won't impact your request latency.
[07:36] Evan: we'd like to run a benchmark with 2k concurrent reqs, p95 target 250ms. what's the input you need?
[07:44] Priya: we'll need a representative prompt set, average token size, concurrency pattern, and preferred QPS distribution. Priya: also confirm model family and quantization level — we can test both fp16 and int8 paths.
[07:58] John: we'll send prompts and call shape. estimate on cost and instance types?
[08:05] Sam: we'll include a ballpark in the checklist. rough guidance — for 2k concurrent with low latency you may need multiple GPU nodes (A100 or H100 depending on model) across AZs. we'll propose config in the follow-up.
[08:19] Maya: about secrets and KMS — we need assurances keys don't leave our account. is that supported?
[08:26] Priya: yes we support CMEK patterns and can do envelope encryption where our service never has your plaintext key. keys stay in your account. we'll include our KMS integration doc.
[08:38] John: audit: we need to ensure retention policies and the ability to pull logs for 12 months. can you meet that?
[08:45] Sam: yep, retention is configurable; longer retention is an add-on but available.
[08:50] Evan: network firewall team will need a diagram and exact CIDRs and FQDNs to allowlist.
[08:57] Priya: we'll provide a network diagram, CIDR ranges, recommended SG rules, and route table changes.
[09:06] John: any blockers for us if we use GCP instead of AWS?
[09:10] Priya: we support private deployment patterns on GCP and Azure as well, but integration specifics differ (VPC peering vs Shared VPC, Private Service Connect on GCP). since you're on AWS primarily, we'll focus on that first.
[09:24] Maya: legal/procurement — we may need a data processing addendum and transfer impact assessment for any cross-border telemetry.
[09:32] Sam: we'll route that to our legal team; priya can attach standard DPA and data residency FAQ.
[09:39] John: ok great. quick question — what's the onboarding timeline for a private deployment?
[09:45] Priya: from kickoff to production typically 4-8 weeks depending on account-level approvals, network setup, and benchmark cycles. if you do bring-your-own-account we can be faster for some parts.
[09:57] Evan: does Redwood provide an AMI or terraform modules for the BYO flow?
[10:03] Priya: yes, we have terraform modules and deployment scripts, plus a terraform provider for infra and an operator for config; we can share the repo links. small note: some managed bits still require config access for scaling.
[10:19] John: any issues with AZ isolation? we run critical services across two AZs and one AZ sometimes has constrained IP quotas.
[10:26] Priya: we will size ENI counts accordingly and recommend requesting quota increases early.
[10:32] Maya: can we enable VPC flow logs for traffic between our pods and Redwood endpoints?
[10:38] Priya: yes, you can enable flow logs on your side; we'll also emit connection logs to your log bucket.
[10:46] Sam: alright wrapping up — recap: Acme wants private VPC in eu-west-1, multi-AZ, p95 < 250ms, 2k concurrency target; security: CMEK/HSM, SAML/Okta, SOC2, audit logs to customer S3, no public internet egress for inference. action items and next steps we'll share.
[11:05] John: sounds good. one last micro question — do you have an offline/install or air-gapped option?
[11:12] Priya: we do offer an on-prem package for highly regulated customers; it's heavier lift but possible. we'll include the matrix in the follow-up.
[11:20] Maya: thanks, we'll look for the checklist.
[11:24] Sam: thanks all, we'll send notes, checklist, pricing, and schedule the benchmark setup.
[11:30] Meeting end.
